short: A long-lived item bought to use rather than to sell.
seoTitle: Fixed Asset — Meaning and Example for Businesses
metaDescription: A fixed asset is a long-lived item bought to be used in the business rather than sold — kitchen equipment, furniture, vehicles, computers, fit-outs.
definition: A fixed asset is a long-lived item bought to be used in the business rather than sold — kitchen equipment, furniture, vehicles, computers, fit-outs. Its cost is recovered through depreciation over its useful life.
bodyHtml:
Why Fixed Asset matters

Fixed assets tie up cash for years, and they quietly disappear from attention once installed. A fixed asset register is the only reliable way to know what you own and what it is now worth.

How Fixed Asset works in practice

Maintain a register with purchase date, cost, location, depreciation method and book value. Verify it physically once a year — small businesses routinely carry assets that were scrapped years ago.

faq.question: What is the difference between a fixed asset and an expense?
faq.answer: An expense is consumed within the period; a fixed asset delivers benefit over several years and is capitalised.

faq.question: Do I need a fixed asset register?
faq.answer: Yes, once you own more than a handful. Insurance, depreciation and disposals all depend on it.
